newsitem.title: QATAR: Gulf states and EU to hold Doha trade talks.
newsitem.headline: Gulf states and EU to hold Doha trade talks.

text.p: Foreign ministers and officials from Gulf Arab states and the European Union will meet in Doha on Monday to discuss ways of boosting trade.

"One of the measures the ministers are expected to discuss is a proposed trade treaty between the two blocs which seeks to eliminate diverse tariffs and trade barriers applied by individual states," a Western diplomat said.

Talks between the EU and Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) states on forging a free trade accord have been blocked over more than 10 years by European Union's demands that GCC states should first unify their tariffs.
The two blocs in April agreed on a time frame of no more than two years to complete the crucial free trade accord which could open European markets for cheap petrochemicals from GCC states.
But differences between some GCC members have for years prevented agreement on the step which is needed for the economic and political alliance to move towards forming a common market.
A final GCC accord on tariffs has been postponed several times.
The GCC -- which includes Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Oman and Bahrain -- is a political and economic alliance.
The diplomat said other topics on the agenda in Monday's talks will include potential transfer of technology and regulations for new joint ventures.
They will also cover business opportunities in the oil-rich Gulf region and efforts to lure foreign investment.
